summary.purpose: clean, previously unexposed held-out bank for the FOCUS-3 ADMISSION screen and the pairwise UPDATER screen, authored because results/open-problem-1-admission-astra.md concludes that no existing bank can certify automatic rule admission: fable-admission/relations-heldout 1-3 are evaluation- and error-analysis-exposed and set 4 had its annotation conventions consumed by the pass3 training repair. Coverage is weighted to the measured miss families (cue-less/terse constraints, multiple rules in one message, constraints after payload or chatter, one-off request versus continuing obligation, withdrawal with replacement, temporal bare values, task overrides of global rules, 'actually B' corrections) plus hard negatives that mimic every one of those shapes.

category_notes.cueless_rule: one standing rule with no from-now-on/always/never/must/whenever phrasing (declaratives, passives, wants, prefers)
category_notes.rule_list: two or three standing rules listed in one sentence, each its own span
category_notes.rule_plus_payload: one standing rule and a one-off payload request in the same message
category_notes.late_rule: the rule arrives after chit-chat or after a data block, never in first position
category_notes.task_override: a task-scoped rule that overrides a live GLOBAL rule of the same key (relation supersedes on the intersection)
category_notes.withdraw_replace: explicit withdrawal plus a replacement in one message ('Drop X; do Y instead')
category_notes.bare_value_temporal: a bare new value carried only by a temporal marker ('Feet and inches from here on.')
category_notes.retire_reinstate: cancels / completes / reinstates; added beyond the named miss families so one bank covers all five pair labels for the updater screen
category_notes.hard_negative: mimics every shape above without changing or adding any rule: formal 'Process request for task X' templates, quoted and reported rule-like text, tool and assistant messages containing rule-like sentences, list-shaped one-off jobs, single-reply exceptions, hedged proposals, wrong-target closures, bare data values and 'actually' corrections of a datum

summary.item_type_notes: admission = admission screen only (old_rule null). relation = pair row whose gold admission annotation is the empty list. both = pair row that also carries admitted spans. standing_rules is gold on ALL 349 rows, so the admission screen can score the whole bank; label/old_rule/target_span are gold on the 175 pair rows.
summary.span_convention: SAME AS fable-admission-heldout-4 (which declares itself SAME AS SET 3): standing_rules spans are verbatim substrings with 0-based [start,end) character offsets into message; a leading framing cue is EXCLUDED from the span ('Two things:', 'Three points for X:', 'Going forward,', 'From now on,', 'For the Marika file', 'On the Ridge Face plan,', 'Actually,', list markers, discourse openers such as 'Anyway,'/'Right,'/'Oh, and', and joining 'and') so the span starts at the first content word of the rule clause and ends before the terminal punctuation; words that carry the rule's content (always, never, no, nothing, not) stay inside the span; a TRAILING marker that belongs to the rule ('from now on', 'from here on', 'going forward') stays INSIDE the span because only a LEADING framing cue is excluded; a matrix predicate of wanting or preferring ('I'd rather', 'We keep') stays inside the span, the conservative reading, because removing it would remove rule content; each list item is its own span; offsets computed by the assembler from the hand-written span text and re-verified by slicing. target_span follows the RELATIONS convention of fable-relations-heldout-4: it is the whole candidate sentence the splitter would supply, verbatim WITH its terminal punctuation, offsets likewise re-verified by slicing.

field_notes.standing_rules: admission-screen gold: every persistent constraint the message states, new key or replacing an existing key; empty when the message admits nothing; tool and assistant rows never carry rules
field_notes.message_new_rule: LABELS-RELATIONS new-KEY flag, false on every pair row here because each positive changes an existing key rather than adding one; true on admission-only rows that state a persistent constraint
field_notes.one_off_request: true when the message asks for a piece of work on data it carries, asks a question, or carries a single-reply-scoped constraint
field_notes.quoted_or_reported: true when rule-shaped text is quoted, reported, hypothetical, tool/assistant-authored, or an assistant acknowledgement
field_notes.old_rule: the single live-or-inactive target the pair row is scored against; version is 1 throughout
field_notes.target_span: the candidate sentence, whole and with terminal punctuation (relations convention)
field_notes.scenario: cab1-<domain>-<topic>; unique per row in this bank

disjointness_receipts.my_units_definition: every distinct message, standing_rules span text, old_rule text, previous_user text, scenario id and domain name in this file
disjointness_receipts.residual_disclosure: the only prior strings that occur anywhere inside this file's units are the three registered temporal cue phrases themselves ('From now on, ', 'Going forward, ', 'going forward'). They are shared vocabulary, not shared items: constraint-TYPE overlap is deliberate and disclosed per LABELS.md, and these cues are the very tokens the cue-less/cued miss-family split is defined by. Zero messages, rule texts, span texts, scenario ids or domain names are shared with any prior file in either direction.
disjointness_receipts.method: mechanical, in a scratchpad script: prior units collected by walking every .jsonl/.json/.md/.sh/.py under data/classifier (model weight directories excluded), parsing JSON rows and extracting quoted strings and whole lines from the .md/.sh/.py files; my units tested for set membership against the prior set, for containment inside a NUL-joined blob of all prior units, and every prior unit of >= 12 characters tested for containment inside a NUL-joined blob of my units; domain and scenario collisions tested pairwise both ways.
disjointness_receipts.not_asserted: key names are a shared taxonomy and were not required or tested to be novel
